This is the global protocol for this repository, flattened from
`.agents/protocol/` so any tool that reads `AGENTS.md` as plain text receives the
always-on content. On-demand modules stay in `.agents/protocol/` and are read
only when a task matches (see "On-Demand Modules" below). To change a rule, edit the relevant module under
`.agents/protocol/` and regenerate this file.

## Protocol Authority

This is the global protocol for this repository. The source of truth is the
module set in `.agents/protocol/`. `.claude/CLAUDE.md` imports those modules with
`@import` (Claude Code expands them at load time). `AGENTS.md` is generated by
flattening the modules that `CLAUDE.md` imports into plain text (run
`python3 .agents/planning/scripts/build_agents.py`) so Codex and opencode, which read
`AGENTS.md` literally, receive the same always-on protocol. On-demand modules are read from
`.agents/protocol/` by every tool.

`.claude/agents/*.md` are Claude Code subagents and the single source of truth
for each role's behavior, triggers, tools, and model. Only the agents installed
there are active; `.agents/agent-catalog/` holds optional agents that project
setup installs when the project needs them.

If the protocol modules and a subagent file ever diverge:

- Follow the protocol modules for repository-wide rules (workflow, token budget, review governance).
- Follow the subagent file for that role's own behavior and limits.
- After editing any module, regenerate `AGENTS.md` with `python3 .agents/planning/scripts/build_agents.py` so it stays in sync with `CLAUDE.md`.

---

## Project Purpose

This repository serves as a reusable base for agent-assisted software work across different project types.

Priorities:

- Correctness.
- Maintainability.
- Clarity.
- Reusability.
- Security.
- Low token usage.

---

## Project Setup Gate

Before any other work, check whether `.agents/context/project_profile.md` exists.

If it does not, the mandatory first task is project setup: read
`.agents/protocol/11-project-setup.md`, ask the user for the project objective
and the tools to be used, and configure the subagents the project needs. Do not
start other non-trivial work until the profile exists.

Skip the gate only when the user states that the work is maintenance of this
template itself rather than a project built from it.

---

## Core Instruction

Do not inspect the whole repository by default.

Use the smallest context required for the task.

Read these first:

1. `.agents/planning/tasks/active_task.md`
2. `.agents/context/current_state.md`
3. The active task's `task.md`

Then read these if present (they are created on demand, not by default):

- `.agents/context/project_profile.md` (objective, tools, installed agents)
- `.agents/context/context_manifest.md`
- `.agents/context/source_map.md`
- `.agents/context/known_decisions.md`

For database tasks, also read `.agents/context/database_map.md` if present.

Then read only files related to the active task.

If a required task or feature file does not exist, create it using the repository conventions.

---

## On-Demand Modules

Not loaded by default (neither imported by `CLAUDE.md` nor inlined in
`AGENTS.md`) to keep the always-on protocol small. Read the file only when the
task matches:

- `.agents/protocol/07-database.md` — any task that changes schema, migrations, persistence, relationships, or important queries.
- `.agents/protocol/08-feature-tracking.md` — when creating or updating a feature folder under `.agents/planning/features/`.
- `.agents/protocol/12-data-ml-rules.md` — Excel/CSV processing, data transformations, or machine-learning work.
- `.agents/protocol/13-review-governance.md` — when performing QA or moving a task to `In Review`.
- `.agents/planning/docs/lessons/{area}.md` — before working in an area, if the file exists (past mistakes and the rule that prevents each).
- `.agents/protocol/11-project-setup.md` — when `.agents/context/project_profile.md` does not exist, or when installing or removing subagents.

---

## Create-On-Demand Rule

Do not create documentation files just because they exist in the convention.

Create a file only when:

- The current task needs it.
- The information will be reused.
- The file helps reduce future context.
- The feature is becoming hard to track.

If a required file does not exist, create it using the standard template.

---

## Task Tracking

Features are larger capabilities: `.agents/planning/features/{id}-{feature-name}/`.

Tasks are units of work that can be implemented, reviewed, and closed
independently: `.agents/planning/tasks/YYYY/MM/{task-id}-{task-name}/`.

`.agents/planning/tasks/active_task.md` is the single pointer to the current task.

Create a task folder when the work:

- Affects more than one file or belongs to a feature.
- Requires QA or review, or may need handoff across sessions.
- Involves database, security, data processing, architecture, or deployment.

Do not create a task folder for trivial one-line or single-file changes unless explicitly requested.

Task files:

- `task.md` — required. One file holds the goal, scope, acceptance criteria, and the QA record. Create it with `python3 .agents/planning/scripts/new_task.py "<title>"`, which picks the next id, copies the template, and updates `active_task.md`.
- `plan.md`, `handoff.md`, `notes.md` — optional; create only when needed.

Every acceptance criterion ends with `verify:` and how it is checked: a command,
a test name, or one concrete manual step. A criterion nobody can check is not a
criterion; rewrite it or drop it.

Do not keep a hand-written list of changed files. Use `git status` and
`git diff --name-only`; they are the record.

Review task rule:

- QA may create a dedicated review task when a follow-up needs a separate specialist pass (`Security`, `Database`, or cross-task QA).
- The review task must record why it was created and which agents must participate.

---

## Statuses and Review Flow

Use only: `Planned`, `In Progress`, `Blocked`, `In Review`, `Done`.

- `Planned`: exists, not started or intentionally postponed.
- `In Progress`: started and expected to continue.
- `Blocked`: started but stopped by a dependency, decision, or external issue.
- `In Review`: implementation complete; QA, and Security if applicable, pending.
- `Done`: implementation, required review, and close-out are complete.

Review flow:

- Implementation completion moves the task to `In Review`, never directly to `Done`.
- QA review is required before `Done`. Read `.agents/protocol/13-review-governance.md` when performing it.
- A non-trivial task cannot move to `Done` while the `## QA` section or the follow-up review decision in `task.md` is incomplete.
- If review finds issues, move the task back to `In Progress` or `Blocked`.

QA review depth:

- `Light`: small local changes with low regression risk.
- `Standard`: normal functional changes, validations, services, operator-facing behavior.
- `Deep`: database, migrations, security-sensitive changes, Excel/CSV, calculations, machine learning, public APIs, or high-regression-risk work.

The lead agent picks the depth from these criteria before delegating to `qa`.
`Light` and `Standard` run on the `qa` default model; for `Deep`, delegate with
the model overridden to opus. If `qa` answers `Escalate to Deep`, re-run it that way.

Security review is required only when the task touches:

- Authentication, authorization, roles, or permissions.
- File upload or file handling.
- Secrets, credentials, or sensitive configuration.
- Public endpoints or externally exposed integrations.
- Sensitive data in fields, logs, errors, or traces.
- Validation or database changes that affect trust boundaries or sensitive fields.

---

## Task Completion Rule

A non-trivial task is not complete until:

- The `## QA` section of `task.md` records checks, findings, tests run or not run, and the follow-up review decision.
- Required Security review is completed when security triggers apply.
- `handoff.md` is written if the task is paused, handed off, or blocked.
- The related feature's `changes_current.md` is updated if behavior changed.
- `.agents/context/current_state.md` is updated only if what is true about the project changed. It is a snapshot: replace the affected lines, do not append history.
- `python3 .agents/planning/scripts/check.py` passes. It runs the project's own checks (`.agents/config/checks.json`) and validates the docs of every `Done` task, and prints only failures.
- `.agents/planning/tasks/active_task.md` shows the final status or the next task.

---

## Token Budget

Default: Low.

### Low

- Max 3 context files.
- Max 2 source files read in full; beyond that, read only targeted slices.
- Before changing a function, type, route, or schema, search for its usages and read the matching slices. A search is cheap; breaking a caller you never saw is not.
- No open-ended exploration.

### Medium

- Max 5 context files.
- Max 5 source files.

### High

Only for architecture, security, database design, major refactors, or complex bugs.

Explain why broader context is needed.

## Token Consumption Strategy

Use these rules to reduce token usage without losing correctness:

- Read in layers: task file first, compact context second, source files last.
- Read slices before full files when headings or targeted sections are enough.
- Activate the fewest agents possible for the current step.
- Delay QA, Security, and DevOps until their trigger conditions are present.
- Prefer updating reusable context files over re-explaining the same state in every task.
- Summarize decisions once in canonical files instead of duplicating them across notes.
- Escalate from `Low` to `Medium` or `High` only when the task risk truly requires it.
- If broader context is used, record why in the task notes or plan.
- Keep agent outputs short and structured; prefer templates and checklists over free-form text.
- Break multi-surface work into smaller tasks so each agent reads less context.

---

## Work Modes

### Fast

Small isolated change.

### Standard

Normal feature work.

### Deep

Architecture, security, database design, major refactor, or complex debugging.

### Review

Do not modify code. Inspect changed files only.

---

## Agent Activation

Use only the agents needed.

| Task Type | Agents |
|---|---|
| Small backend fix | Backend, QA |
| Small frontend fix | Frontend, QA |
| New API endpoint | Architect, Backend, QA, Security |
| New database table | Database, Backend, QA, Security |
| Database relationship change | Database, Backend, QA |
| Migration | Database, Backend, QA, Security if sensitive data is involved |
| File upload | Architect, Backend, Security, Database if metadata is persisted, QA |
| Excel/CSV transformation | Data, Backend, QA, Database if results are persisted |
| Machine learning | Machine Learning, Data, QA, Database if predictions or model runs are stored |
| AI API or automation integration | AI Integrations, Backend, QA, Security if external exposure or sensitive data is involved |
| Dashboard | Frontend, Backend, QA, Database if new queries or tables are needed |
| Deployment | DevOps, Security, Database if migrations or persistence are involved |
| Refactor | Architect, QA, Database if persistence changes |
| Context cleanup | Context |

Role labels in this table are Claude Code subagents in `.claude/agents/`. Some
labels differ from the file name: Data → `data-analytics`, Frontend →
`frontend-ui`, Context → `context-manager`. Delegate to them by subagent name.

Only agents installed in `.claude/agents/` can be delegated to. If the table
calls for a role that is not installed, install it from `.agents/agent-catalog/`
(see `11-project-setup.md`) or have the lead agent cover that step and record
the gap in the task notes.

Do not activate all agents by default.

Default activation rule:

- Start with the smallest useful set.
- Add Architect only for new features, cross-module design, or large refactors.
- Add DevOps only for deployment, CI/CD, runtime environment, or production execution concerns.
- Add Innovation only when the goal is to propose improvements, simplifications, or operational efficiencies without blocking current delivery.

Activation limits:

- `Fast`: max 2 active agents.
- `Standard`: max 3 active agents.
- `Deep`: activate extra agents only with a concrete risk-based reason.
- `Review`: only review agents and changed files.

Stage ownership rule:

- Each task stage must have one lead agent.
- Supporting agents join only when a documented trigger is hit.
- When the lead agent changes, leave a structured handoff instead of repeating full context.

---

## Delegation for Token Efficiency

Prefer delegating to a subagent over reading in the main thread when a step is
read-heavy or exploratory, so file contents stay in the subagent's isolated
context and only the conclusion returns to the main thread.

Delegate when:

- A step needs reading many files or a wide search to answer one question.
- The work is self-contained and can be specified in a short brief.
- A specialist role (per the activation table) clearly owns the step.

Keep in the main thread when:

- The change touches 1-2 known files (delegation overhead is not worth it).
- The step needs the full conversation context to be correct.

When delegating, give the subagent: the goal, the acceptance criteria, the
relevant project state in two or three lines, the exact files or search scope,
and the expected return shape (a short summary or a diff, never raw file dumps).
A brief that carries this replaces the subagent's own reading of the task and
context files. The reply must be the conclusion, not the contents read. One delegation depth
per step; no recursive delegation by default.

---

## Agent Roles

Full role specifications live as Claude Code subagents in `.claude/agents/*.md`.
That directory is the single source of truth for each role's purpose, triggers,
rules, limitations, tools, and model. The main agent delegates to a subagent by
name (see the activation table in Work Modes); each subagent runs in its own
isolated context, so its work does not consume the main thread's tokens.

Do not duplicate role specifications here. Update the subagent file instead.

`qa`, `security`, and `context-manager` are core and always installed. The other
roles ship in `.agents/agent-catalog/` and are installed into `.claude/agents/`
by project setup (`11-project-setup.md`) according to the project's objective
and tools.

Role label (used in the activation table and in QA `review_agents`) → subagent:

| Role label | Subagent | Model | Installed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Architect | `architect` | opus | on setup |
| Backend | `backend` | sonnet | on setup |
| Database | `database` | opus | on setup |
| Data | `data-analytics` | sonnet | on setup |
| Machine Learning | `machine-learning` | opus | on setup |
| AI Integrations | `ai-integrations` | sonnet | on setup |
| Frontend | `frontend-ui` | sonnet | on setup |
| QA | `qa` | sonnet (opus for `Deep`) | core |
| Security | `security` | opus | core |
| DevOps | `devops` | sonnet | on setup |
| Context | `context-manager` | haiku | core |
| Innovation | `innovation` | haiku | on setup |
| (optional UI critic) | `ux-operational` | haiku | on setup |

---

Areas and review lines are defined in `.agents/config/org.json`; the chart in
`README.md` is generated from it with `python3 .agents/planning/scripts/build_org.py`.
Areas only group roles: the lead agent delegates directly to each specialist.

Review governance (QA scheduling, non-negotiable triggers, proportionality, the
`other` rationale) lives in `.agents/protocol/13-review-governance.md`, read on
demand when performing QA.

## Development Methodology

Use this repository workflow for normal delivery:

1. Start from the core reading order. Activate `Context` only when the reading path is unclear, the context has grown large, or work is drifting into unrelated files.
2. Open or point to a task when the work is non-trivial or crosses files.
3. Assign one lead agent for the current stage and keep other agents inactive unless triggered.
4. Add specialist agents only when their trigger conditions are reached.
5. When ownership changes, write a short structured handoff instead of re-explaining full context.
6. Record reusable decisions in shared context or feature files instead of repeating them in chat.
7. Move the task to `In Review` after implementation, then run QA from diff, acceptance criteria, and nearby regression risk.
8. During QA, explicitly decide whether a dedicated follow-up review task is needed and record the rationale.
9. If a follow-up review is needed, create a new review task and assign the required review agents and depth.
10. Run Security or Database review directly only when QA determines a separate review task is unnecessary and the protocol still requires a local pass.
11. Run `python3 .agents/planning/scripts/check.py` before closing a non-trivial task; read only what it reports as failed.
12. Move to `Done` only after tracking, QA, validation, and any scheduled follow-up reviews are complete.

Test-first rule: for `Standard` and `Deep` tasks in a project with a test runner,
write the failing test from the acceptance criteria before the implementation.
Let machines check what machines can check (`check.py`); spend review effort on
whether the task solved what was asked, edge cases, and risk.

---

## Documentation Rule

Documentation is not a default agent.

Use documentation as a closing responsibility when:

- A decision will be reused.
- A schema change requires traceability.
- A feature is becoming hard to track.

Rules:

- Document decisions, not conversations.
- Avoid duplication.
- Update only relevant docs.
- Keep docs short.

---

## No-Go Rules

Do not:

- Read unrelated files.
- Read the whole repository by default.
- Refactor unrelated code.
- Rewrite full files unnecessarily.
- Rename files without clear reason.
- Add dependencies without justification.
- Read archive files unless required.
- Paste full files in responses.
- Explain general concepts unless asked.
- Track non-trivial work only in feature docs without task-level tracking.
- Keep hand-written lists of changed files; git is the record.
- Duplicate full feature context inside task files.
- Modify database schema without migration and documentation.
- Add database relationships without justification.

---

## Review Severity

- P0: Critical — security issue, data loss, production-breaking bug.
- P1: High — core functionality broken or incorrect result.
- P2: Medium — maintainability issue, missing validation, weak edge case.
- P3: Low — style, naming, minor cleanup.

Focus on P0-P2.

---

## Expected Final Response

For normal implementation tasks, return only:

1. Files changed.
2. Summary.
3. Tests.
4. Risks.

For database tasks, return only:

1. Files changed.
2. Database changes.
3. Backend integration changes.
4. Tests.
5. Risks.

For reviews, return only:

1. Findings.
2. Required changes.
3. Suggested tests.
4. Final recommendation.

Do not include long explanations unless explicitly requested.
